مِسْكٌ نَفَّاحٌ [Musk that diffuses much odour or fragrance]. (A, art. خطر.) ＝
-A2- طَعْنَةٌ نَفَّاحَةٌ (tropical:) A
stab that ejects, or spirts forth, blood, much, or vehemently. (TA.) ↓ طَعْنَةٌ نَفُوحٌ (tropical:) A stab that ejects its blood quickly. (T.) ＝
-A3- نَفَّاحٌ (tropical:) One who gives many gifts. (TA.) ―
-b2- النَّفَّاحُ, (K,) or النَّفَّاحُ بِالخَيْرِ, (TA,) The Bestower of [many] benefits upon mankind, or the creation: (K:) an epithet applied to God; but disapproved by some, because not so applied in the Kur-án or the traditions.
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
